verdict: Avoid new pharma/API exposure in Puducherry for now; lend only to licensed, compliance-clean formulation or CDMO units with verified export orders and tight monthly monitoring.
title: Puducherry Pharmaceuticals & APIs: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**A Puducherry pharma unit buys APIs and excipients, converts them into formulations or contract batches, and sells into domestic trade or export.** Cash is tied up in raw-material inventory and in receivables from distributors and overseas buyers; the plant itself is the smaller part of the balance sheet. **The value sits in regulatory approvals and customer qualification, not in the machinery** — which is why a licence cancellation can wipe out a unit overnight. Note the December 2025 crackdown: the Drugs Control Department cancelled licences and sealed several firms for violations in sale, storage and distribution [2]. So when a proposal lands, check the current drug licence and any suspension history first; if the licence status is unclear, ask for the department's written confirmation before anything else. ## What has changed now
**The local demand signal is weak.** Puducherry GST collections are down 20.7% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1%, and electricity demand is up only 6.1% versus India's 9.5% [D]. Nationally, output is -2.1% Apr-to-date while bank credit is +21.6% YoY [D] — money is chasing a shrinking production base, so weak borrowers will look creditworthy on paper. That is a local news claim from FIEO, not audited data — treat it as direction, not proof. ## Where the growth is
**Peer results show the API/CDMO end is where the money is being made.** Aarti Pharmalabs reported record quarterly revenue of ₹613 crore, up 47% YoY, with EBITDA margin at 22.2% [4][6]. RPG Life Sciences is targeting 25% API growth and eyeing another acquisition within 12 months [5]. **Pursue Puducherry units that are genuine contract manufacturers or API suppliers with named export buyers and clean licences.** Avoid pure traders and storage/distribution outfits — that is exactly the segment the crackdown hit [2]. ## How to grow safely
**Structure against the working-capital cycle, because that is where these firms die.** Rating reports show working-capital intensity of 47-52% at one API peer [10] and high customer concentration at another [8]. So take monthly stock-and-debtor statements, not quarterly; if receivables cross the sanctioned cycle, ask for the buyer-wise ageing. **Take the drug licence renewal date, GST returns and top-five buyer concentration every month.** Where exports fund repayment, insist on export-realisation routing through the bank. ## Early-warning signs
- **GST turnover falling faster than the Puducherry average of -20.7% [D] (monthly)** -> stop fresh disbursement and review the limit. - **Any licence show-cause or sealing notice [2] (event-based)** -> freeze the account and call the promoter. - **Top buyer crossing a third of sales [8] (quarterly)** -> ask for a second-buyer order book before renewal. - **Inventory days rising while sales fall [10] (monthly)** -> shift to stock-backed limits only.
